entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Carl Hindrik Sven Rudolphsson Lidman —military officer, poet, writer, and preacher, grandson of the priest Sven Lidman—was born in Karlskrona, became a sublieutenant in the Swedish royal army reserve in 1903, and studied law at Uppsala University. He then began a promising career as a celebrated poet with Pasiphaë (1904), Primavera (1905), Källorna (1906), and Elden och altaret (1907). He also wrote the dramas Imperia (1907) and Härskare (1908), before starting to write novels: Stensborg (1910), Thure Gabriel Silfverstååhl (1910), Carl Silfverstååhls upplevelser, Köpmän och krigare, Tvedräktens barn (1913), and Det levande fäderneshuset (1916).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a celebrated poet and writer, Sven Lidman's works had a significant impact on Swedish literature during the early 20th century, with his novels and dramas being widely read and studied. His writing career spanned over two decades, leaving a lasting legacy in the literary world of Northern Europe.
